skill.name: ai-rag-pipeline
skill.description: Build retrieval augmented generation workflows that combine web search, content extraction, and LLM analysis through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.summary: Create grounded research and fact-checking pipelines with search, extraction, and LLM synthesis.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms a critical pipe-to-shell installer pattern in the Quick Start and a related hardcoded installer URL. Most other static hits are Markdown formatting, illustrative infsh examples, placeholder URLs, or documentation links rather than hidden execution paths.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the Quick Start with a manual download, checksum verification, and a command that executes only the verified local binary.

remediation.issue: Examples rely on external search and LLM services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear data handling note so users avoid submitting secrets, credentials, regulated data, or private documents.

remediation.issue: Several shell examples interpolate variables into JSON strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use a JSON builder or validated input files in examples so quotes in topics cannot break request payloads.

content.value_statement: Research agents need current sources and clear attribution. This skill shows how to combine search, extraction, and LLM synthesis through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Shows search plus LLM patterns using Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter app IDs.
Demonstrates multi-source research, URL extraction, fact-checking, and report generation flows.
Includes examples for summarizing long search results before deeper analysis.
Documents source attribution practices for grounded responses.
Lists related inference.sh skills and documentation links for extended workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, login, and network access.
Does not provide local indexing, vector database setup, or embedding storage.
Results depend on third-party search, extraction, and LLM services.
Example shell snippets may need adaptation for production error handling.

use_cases.title: Create Cited Research Briefs
use_cases.description: Use search results and LLM synthesis to prepare concise briefs with source attribution.

use_cases.title: Compare Market Signals
use_cases.description: Gather multiple search results, identify shared themes, and surface contradictions for planning decisions.

use_cases.title: Draft Grounded Support Answers
use_cases.description: Retrieve current documentation or article content before generating answers for knowledge workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Grounded Answer
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting with one research question.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-rag-pipeline skill to design a simple search plus Claude answer flow for this question: [question]. Include source attribution.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you need balanced research from more than one search provider.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a multi-source RAG workflow for [topic]. Search with Tavily and Exa, compare findings, and note contradictions.

prompt_templates.title: Fact-Check a Claim
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a claim needs evidence and a clear verdict.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fact-checking pipeline to evaluate this claim: [claim]. Return a verdict, supporting evidence, conflicting evidence, and sources.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Research Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when building a reusable advanced workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable RAG pipeline for [domain]. Include retrieval steps, extraction, summarization strategy, citation requirements, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a current market overview of electric vehicles.
output: A research plan with Tavily and Exa searches.
A synthesized summary of trends, risks, and open questions.
A source list that separates cited facts from interpretation.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether a public claim is supported by evidence.
output: A clear claim verdict with confidence language.
Supporting and contradicting evidence grouped by source.
A note when evidence is weak, outdated, or incomplete.

output_examples.input: A user asks to turn two URLs into an analysis brief.
output: Extracted document themes and key facts.
Source attribution for each major claim.

best_practices: Use specific queries with dates, entities, and context to improve retrieval quality.
Ask the model to separate sourced facts from interpretation.
Review generated citations before sharing outputs with users or teams.
anti_patterns: Do not submit secrets, credentials, or private documents to external services.
Do not treat search snippets as verified facts without source review.
Do not run remote installer scripts without local inspection and checksum verification.

faq.question: Does this skill build a full vector database?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on search, extraction, and LLM synthesis patterns through inference.sh.

faq.question: Which services does it reference?
faq.answer: It references Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter-hosted models, including Claude, GPT-4o, and Gemini examples.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code supported tool surfaces.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows depend on external search, extraction, and LLM provider calls.

faq.question: Can it fact-check claims?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a pipeline pattern for gathering evidence and producing a sourced verdict.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Do not send confidential data unless your organization approves the external providers involved.
